references.text: The continuation of the Nazirite's separation from the dead, which includes even close family members such as father, mother, brother, or sister.
Men who became unclean by touching a corpse and therefore could not celebrate Passover at the proper time show how contact with the dead made one unclean.
The laws about uncleanness through touching a corpse, explaining why the Nazirite had to stay away from the dead.
The priests' prohibition against making themselves unclean by the dead, except for close relatives. The Nazirite had even stricter requirements.
The high priest was not allowed to go near any corpse, not even his father or mother, corresponding to the Nazirite's strict requirements.
Ezekiel's laws for priests regarding uncleanness from the dead, reflecting the principles of the Nazirite vow.
The prohibition against cutting oneself for the dead, showing respect for life and separation from death.
